LOOP ENGINEERING MASTERCLASS
MOHIT'S CONVERSATIONAL, SLIDE-BY-SLIDE TALK TRACK

Use this as a speaking guide, not a script to memorise. Keep the meaning, look at the audience, and speak in your own rhythm.

YOUR FLOW

Slides 1-4: You open, introduce Interview Kickstart, and bring in Jeevendra.
Slides 5-28: Jeevendra presents.
Slides 29-37: You return for the program conversation.
Slides 38-50: Jeevendra continues.
End: You take it back and close.

============================================================
SLIDE 1 - LOOP ENGINEERING
============================================================

So today's session is about something most of us don't really think about.

We ask an AI model to do something. It gives us an answer. And usually, we stop there.

But what if that answer has to go into a real product or reach a real customer?

Who checks whether it is actually right?

If it is wrong, what tells the model what went wrong?

Does it try again? And how many times should it try before it stops?

That entire part after the first answer is what today's session is about. That is loop engineering.

Jeevendra is going to take us through four different kinds of loops and show how this works through live examples as well.

Just quickly, how many of you already use an AI coding tool regularly? Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, anything. Just drop the name in the chat.

[Read two or three responses.]

Nice. Then you will be able to connect a lot of today's discussion to things you have already seen while using these tools.

We also have 18 different role-based curricula. So a backend engineer, a data professional, and an engineering manager do not get pushed through exactly the same journey.

That is really the idea behind IK. Keep the learning close to what people are building in the industry and what companies are actually hiring for.

AFTER SLIDE 28 - BRIDGE BACK TO YOUR SECTION
============================================================

Guys, I am just going to borrow the screen for the next few minutes, and then I will hand it straight back to Jeevendra.

What we just saw is actually very important from a career point of view as well.

Building something once and seeing it run is one level. Being able to check it, improve it, and make it dependable is a very different level of capability.

And this is where many people get confused. They know they need to learn AI, but they do not know how deep they need to go, where they should start, or which role would even make sense for them.

So let me quickly make that part simpler.


============================================================
SLIDE 29 - WHAT DO WE MEAN BY A 10X PROFESSIONAL?
============================================================

Now, 10x professional sounds a little dramatic. I know.

We do not mean that you should work ten times more or write ten times more code.

We mean that AI gives you more leverage. You can take on a larger problem, move faster, and own more of the outcome.

But that only happens when you know what to do beyond the first AI-generated answer.

Can you test it? Can you improve it? Can you put it into production? Can you explain the trade-offs to another engineer or even to a customer?

That is where the real value starts showing up.


============================================================
SLIDE 30 - WHY PEOPLE GET STUCK
============================================================

Now tell me honestly. Which one of these have you thought at some point?

One - AI is moving too fast. I will never be able to catch up.

Two - there is simply too much. I do not know where to begin.

Three - my role is quite specialised, so maybe I am safe for now.

Or four - if I move into AI, I may have to start my career again from a lower level.

Just type 1, 2, 3, or 4 in the chat. No explanation needed.

[Pause and react.]

Okay, so clearly a lot of people are thinking about the same things.

The good news is that you do not have to throw away the experience you already have. Your experience is actually your starting point.

The question is simply: what new AI capability should you add to it?


============================================================
SLIDE 31 - FINDING YOUR PLACE ON THE AI CURVE
============================================================

This is the easiest way to look at it.

The first stage is being comfortable with LLMs. Most of us have already started doing this.

The second stage is using copilots properly in our daily work. This is mainly about productivity.

The third stage is when you begin building GenAI applications and agents. Today's session sits largely in this area. Once the agent starts taking actions, questions around loops, verification, and guardrails become important.

Then you have modern ML and deep ML. Those are more specialised paths.

Everyone in technology should probably understand the first two stages. But everyone does not need to become a deep ML engineer.

Your right starting point depends on what you do today and what you want to do next.


============================================================
SLIDE 32 - WHICH PATH SOUNDS LIKE YOU?
============================================================

Now, where do our programs fit into this?

There are two pathways on the screen.

If you are thinking, "Mohit, I understand that AI is important, but honestly, I am still not sure where I fit," then look at the path on the left.

That is Transformative GenAI and Agentic AI along with Interview Lab.

It takes you from GenAI foundations into agents and multi-agent systems. Then the interview preparation gets mapped to the role you want to target. There are 18 role tracks, so this can work differently for a software engineer, an EM, a PM, a TPM, a data professional, or someone from SRE or DevOps.

You also build an enterprise capstone, or you can bring a suitable project of your own.

Now, if you are already clear and your response is, "I specifically want to move towards a Forward Deployed AI Engineering role," then look at the path on the right.

That path is much more focused. It combines AI engineering with the actual FDE work of understanding a customer problem, designing the solution, building it, deploying it, and then driving adoption.

It runs across 23 weeks and includes two capstones that simulate that complete journey.

So the left side gives you broader AI capability plus role-specific interview preparation. The right side is for a focused transition into FDE.

And whichever path you look at, today's lesson remains relevant. Getting a model to produce something is only the beginning. The real work is making that system reliable enough for people to use.


============================================================
SLIDE 33 - INTERVIEW PREPARATION BY ROLE
============================================================

Once you choose a target role, the preparation also has to change.

A backend engineer will not face the same interview as an engineering manager. A data engineer, SRE, test engineer, or TPM will each be evaluated differently.

That is why you see so many tracks here.

We do not expect you to prepare for everything on this slide. We help you pick the relevant track and focus on the coding, system design, domain knowledge, or leadership areas that matter for that role.


============================================================
SLIDE 34 - WHAT THE PREPARATION LOOKS LIKE
============================================================

Then comes the practice part.

The Interview Lab includes DSA, system design, and preparation for your specific domain.

You also get 15 live mock interviews. These are proper simulated interviews, followed by written and verbal feedback.

The idea is that you should discover your weak patterns during practice, not during the actual interview.

The career services side helps with your LinkedIn profile, resume, behavioural interviews, and offer negotiation as well.

So it covers both parts: becoming capable for the role and then being able to present that capability properly during the hiring process.


============================================================

Now, one quick point on placement assistance because I want to be very clear about what it means.

We have more than 200 hiring partners in India. Opportunities can also come through the alumni network and relevant instructor referrals.

But referrals are based on your performance and your fit for the role. It is not an automatic placement guarantee.

The team helps open the right doors once you are ready. You still have to clear the interview process.

============================================================
QUICK DECK CHECKS BEFORE GOING LIVE
============================================================

1. Slide 32 says "Three paths," but only two paths are shown. Change it to "Two paths."
2. Slide 33 repeats the number 8, and its title overlaps the logo.
3. Slide 5 breaks the word "Agenda" into two lines.
4. The existing presenter notes on Slides 32, 34, and 35 belong to an older session. Do not use them.
5. Slide 37 shows "50% refund*" without displaying the conditions. Keep the exact eligibility terms ready if someone asks.
